title: Integration: register comms toolkit in McpHttpServer merged layer AND supply live ChannelGateway (boss1 yyd symbols) in ONE change; remove the 'comms granted while surface empty' state
description: Deferred from PR #1 (boss3 chose not to register a toolkit whose gateway has no implementation). Acceptance: (1) apps/server/src/mcp/McpHttpServer.ts merged layer includes the comms toolkit registration exported from toolkits/comms; (2) ChannelGatewayLive implemented against boss1's channel aggregate (decider/projection from t3_bot-yyd) with typed errors; (3) an integration test drives a real Claude or Codex session's MCP tool list and asserts comms_post/comms_reply/comms_read_channel are present and callable; (4) ProviderService agentAccessCapabilities 'comms' grant is now backed by a live surface. A test that passes with the registration line removed is tautological.
notes:
READ-SIDE IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (boss3, checked against origin/boss1/t3_bot-yyd-channel-decider):

readPosts must OVER-FETCH BY ONE. The gateway contract says nextCursor is null when no newer posts exist. boss1's listPosts returns up to `limit` rows and nothing else - no total, no has-more - so the obvious implementation

  nextCursor = rows.length === limit ? cursorOf(rows.at(-1)) : null

is wrong on an exactly-full final page: four posts at limit 2 hands back a cursor after post-4 and the next call returns empty. Ask the repository for limit + 1, return limit, set nextCursor only if the extra row came back.

This needs a GATEWAY-LEVEL test over the real repository. handlers.test.ts:411 already pins the strict contract, but it passes today only because the in-memory fake knows the total and answers exactly (handlers.test.ts:143). A naive live gateway would satisfy every handler test and violate the contract those tests exist to protect - the fake cannot have the bug, so it cannot catch it.

ALSO CONFIRMED AT THE SEAM, no work needed: ChannelMember is handle/memberKind/memberId exactly; ChannelAuthorRef matches; getPost is channel-scoped on both sides; paging is oldest-first ascending by sequence with `sequence > afterSequence`, which is the contract's "cursor points AFTER the last post returned". createPost is correctly absent from the repository - it goes through the command path, which is the half that waits on a44.

MEMBERSHIP FILTERING LANDS HERE. boss1's getChannelByName deliberately does NOT filter by membership, so getChannelForMember does the test itself: fetch by name, then require a member with memberKind "thread" and memberId === threadId. Keep non-member and missing collapsed into one Option.none branch (t3_bot-glu).

NAME MATCHING IS UNSPECIFIED IN THE GATEWAY DOCSTRING and the two sides currently disagree - see t3_bot-2x5. State the rule here regardless of which way the SQL goes.

Channel name lookup and uniqueness are case-sensitive; two case-variants can coexist
description:
Found by reading boss1's ProjectionChannels (origin/boss1/t3_bot-yyd-channel-decider) against the merged channelGateway contract, before either side lands.

PROVEN, NOT REASONED. The lookup is byte-exact and so is the uniqueness constraint:

  findChannelByName: sql`${selectChannelColumns} WHERE name = ${name}`
  051_ProjectionChannels: name TEXT NOT NULL; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON projection_channels (name)

No COLLATE on either. Executed in sqlite:
  INSERT 'Seniors'; INSERT 'seniors';   -> rows: 2      (the unique index does not stop it)
  SELECT ... WHERE name = 'SENIORS'     -> <none>

TWO CONSEQUENCES.
1. normalizeChannelName (handlers.ts:28) strips the leading sigil and trims but does not fold case, so a channel stored as "seniors" is unreachable to an agent that types "#Seniors".
2. The index comment says "Unique because a mention names one channel". It does not: two channels differing only in case coexist and are mentioned separately.

WHY IT IS HARDER TO DIAGNOSE THAN IT LOOKS. A failed name lookup returns CommsChannelNotFoundError, which is deliberately the same answer a non-member gets so an agent cannot probe for channels it is not in. That conflation is correct and it means an agent with the case wrong cannot distinguish it from exclusion. Related: t3_bot-glu.

THE ROOT AMBIGUITY IS IN THE GATEWAY, which is mine. channelGateway.ts documents the field as "canonical name, without the leading #" and never says whether matching folds case. Two sides implementing an unstated rule is how they disagree.

OPTIONS:
(a) COLLATE NOCASE on the name column and the unique index. One place, fixes lookup and uniqueness together, no second column to keep in sync. LIMIT: SQLite NOCASE folds ASCII A-Z only, so non-ASCII names still compare byte-exact. Honest partial fix.
(b) Store a folded name_key for lookup and uniqueness, keep the display name separate. Complete, costs a column and a rule about which one every query uses.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the wrong fix fails):
1. Whichever option is chosen, the GATEWAY DOCSTRING must state the matching rule explicitly. A fix that changes only the SQL leaves the next implementer of that seam free to disagree again.
2. A test must prove two channels differing only in case CANNOT both be created. Asserting that the lookup is case-insensitive is not enough - it passes while the uniqueness hole stays open, and the hole is the half that makes a mention ambiguous.
3. A test must prove a channel created in one case is reachable from another, THROUGH the handler, not by calling the repository. The normalizer is on the handler side and a repository-level test cannot see it.
4. If option (a), state the non-ASCII limitation in the migration comment. A comment claiming the index makes a mention name one channel must be true or gone.

Blocks the 0uq read side only in the sense that the gateway docstring is written there; the SQL decision is boss1's, on yyd, which has not merged.
notes:
PM RULING 2026-09-11 22:39, supersedes the options in the description:

CANONICAL = lowercase, leading # stripped, trimmed. Normalisation happens in the DECIDER (channel.create and every lookup by name), so the projection only ever stores lowercase and the existing plain unique index is correct as-is. NO COLLATE NOCASE - one rule in one place beats a SQL-level rule the next reader has to know about. The toolkit normalises too, for agent-readable errors, but the decider is the guarantee. Handles follow the same rule.

Also settles the non-ASCII limitation I raised: folding in the decider is JS toLowerCase, which handles more than SQLite's NOCASE (ASCII A-Z only). The ruling is strictly better than the option I recommended.

SPLIT OF WORK:
- boss1, on yyd: apply in the decider if it is a one-line change; otherwise it lands here after a44.
- boss3: gateway docstring must say "canonical = lowercase, no sigil" (channelGateway.ts, the Channel.name field and getChannelForMember). Plus normalizeChannelName and normalizeHandle in handlers.ts must fold case.

NOT A ONE-LINE CHANGE ON MY SIDE, and the criteria below still apply. Lowercasing normalizeHandle changes what comms_read_channel reports as member handles (handlers.ts:235 normalises the member list it returns) and what resolveMentions echoes back in `mentioned`. Existing assertions in handlers.test.ts cover both. Any mixed-case fixture has to be re-read rather than mechanically lowercased, or the tests will be updated to match the new behaviour instead of checking it - which is the tautological-test trap.

Deadline: must land before M1's demo. PM: "I will type #Seniors on purpose."

Criterion 1 in the description is now partly satisfied by the ruling itself, but the docstring change is still required - the rule has to be readable at the seam, not only in a board message.

title: Channel name uniqueness is enforced only by a SQL index, surfacing as a persistence error with no rejected receipt
description:
Found by the bug-hunter lane on PR #4 (BUG-1), confidence 92 / impact 3, executed not reasoned.

The decider checks channel EXISTENCE by id (requireChannelAbsent) but never checks NAME uniqueness. Migration 051 has CREATE UNIQUE INDEX projection_channels_name, and the upsert conflicts on channel_id only, so it never covers that index.

OBSERVED: creating a second channel with a name already taken gives 'createDuplicateName decider: Success', then the projection write fails with 'UNIQUE constraint failed: projection_channels.name'.

Why that matters beyond the error text: it rolls back cleanly inside the engine transaction, but it surfaces as PersistenceSqlError rather than an invariant error, so isOrchestrationCommandRejection is FALSE and NO rejected receipt is written. Every other rejection in this engine writes one, and that receipt is what makes a replay of the same commandId short-circuit. So this failure mode is inconsistent with the rest of the command surface.

Second effect: a channel name can never be REUSED after archiving, because nothing deletes the row. Archive is not delete, so 'seniors' is permanently taken once created.

FIX DIRECTION: add requireChannelNameAbsent in commandInvariants.ts, mirroring the existing requireActiveProjectWorkspaceRootAbsent which solves exactly this shape for project workspace roots (same file). It must cover channel.create AND channel.meta.update (rename onto a taken name has the same failure). Decide at the same time whether an archived channel's name is reusable - if yes, the invariant scopes to non-archived channels, exactly as requireActiveProjectWorkspaceRootAbsent scopes to non-deleted projects.

ACCEPTANCE (observable): creating or renaming onto a taken name is rejected with an OrchestrationCommandInvariantError whose detail names the conflict, a rejected receipt IS written, and a second dispatch of the same commandId short-circuits on that receipt.

NOT fixed in PR #4: it is a new invariant plus a decision about archived-name reuse, and #4 is already carrying two review fixes. The SQL index means the bad state cannot actually be written today - the failure is the error shape and the missing receipt, not corruption.
notes:
BLAST RADIUS SETTLED BY EXECUTION, not by either reading. Test committed at ff69288fe:
apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationEngine.test.ts, "a duplicate channel name fails one command, not the engine".

OBSERVED against a real database and a real engine:
  create "seniors"                      -> Success
  create "seniors" again, different id  -> Failure
  create "project" AFTER the failure    -> Success
  read model                            -> ["project", "seniors"]

So the security lane rated it impact 5 on "blast radius is the whole server" and that half is WRONG. A typed
PersistenceSqlError raised INSIDE the Effect fails one command and leaves the engine serving, exactly as an
unroutable command does. Only a defect raised OUTSIDE the Effect killed the worker, and that was the l8i bug,
fixed in 8660c7933.
Verified the test is not vacuous: dropping UNIQUE from the name index turns it RED.

WHAT IS STILL REAL, and why this stays P1 rather than dropping back to P2:
- The decider says Success for a command the projection then refuses, so the failure surfaces as a persistence
  error rather than an invariant error.
- isOrchestrationCommandRejection is FALSE for a SQL error, so NO rejected receipt is written. Every other
  rejection in this engine writes one, and that receipt is what makes a retry of the same commandId
  short-circuit. So this command re-processes on every retry.
- All projectors share one transaction (ProjectionPipeline.ts:2146-2162), so the failed write rolls back the
  cursor advance for every projector on that event - which is correct behaviour for a failed command, but
  means the cost is not confined to the channel projector.

MORE REACHABLE AFTER 868e9af3f, not less: canonicalising names to lowercase means "#Seniors" and "seniors"
now collide as ONE name where they previously produced two rows.

FIX unchanged: requireChannelNameAbsent in the decider, mirroring requireActiveProjectWorkspaceRootAbsent,
covering channel.create AND channel.meta.update. Decide at the same time whether an archived channel frees
its name - archive is not delete, so today a name is taken permanently once created.

title: Channel command edge cases: archive/unarchive state guard, no-op meta.update, unvalidated limit, unvalidated parentPostId, posts into archived channels
notes:
Five Suggestion findings from the bug-hunter lane on PR #4, grouped because they share one shape: a channel command that should be a no-op or a rejection instead emits an event.

BUG-4 decider.ts ~2065 archive/unarchive have NO state guard. Archiving an already-archived channel emits another channel.archived. thread.archive has requireThreadArchived/requireThreadNotArchived in the same file.

BUG-5 decider.ts ~2046 channel.meta.update with no fields set emits an event carrying only channelId and updatedAt. It still costs a sequence number, a projection write, and a wake.

BUG-6 Services/ProjectionChannels.ts:52 listPosts takes limit unvalidated. The seam says 1..200 enforced at the tool schema, so the repository trusts a caller it does not control. In SQLite LIMIT -1 means NO LIMIT: an unbounded read of a whole channel history.

BUG-7 decider.ts ~2150 parentPostId is never validated. A reply can name a parent that does not exist or lives in another channel. getPost was added to the seam for exactly this check and the decider does not use it. Note the decider cannot see posts by design, so the check belongs at the gateway - that is the interesting half.

BUG-8 decider.ts ~2150 posts are accepted into an ARCHIVED channel. Decide what archive is for: read-only means post.create must reject; UI filter means say so where the next person reads it.

COMMON THREAD: four of five are guards that already exist for threads in the same file. I built the channel aggregate by pattern-matching the SHAPE of the thread cases without carrying over their INVARIANTS. Read commandInvariants.ts's thread helpers first and port the set deliberately.

ACCEPTANCE (observable): for each, dispatch the offending command and assert the outcome - rejection or no event - not that a guard function exists.

Post→turn trigger: event-log subscriber enqueues a turn on mention
description: Post->turn reactor. Subscribes to channel post-created events (subscribeDomainEvents); for each mentioned member of kind thread, dispatches thread.turn.start on that thread with the post as input. NEVER enqueues on the thread that authored the post. Acceptance: (1) integration test against the real engine: a post mentioning @boss1 enqueues exactly one turn on boss1's thread and zero on the author's; (2) a post with no thread mentions enqueues nothing; (3) when the enqueued turn is cancelled (compaction failure, interrupt, session stop) the cancellation reaches the post: correlate post -> messageId -> the error activity carrying requestId, and surface it on the post (j6o: correlation is by post/mention id, never turnId); a test asserting only that a turn was enqueued is tautological; (4) the toolkit is registered in McpHttpServer's live layer by 0uq before this ships, so the woken agent can reply with comms_post.

Channel membership and authorship have no authorization: any caller can post as anyone, self-add, or evict
description:
Found by the security lane on PR #4 (t3_bot-yyd), SEC-1 and SEC-2, both confidence 98 / HIGH, both EXECUTED against the real decider rather than reasoned about.

SEC-1 - AUTHORSHIP IS FORGEABLE. channel.post.create carries authorRef and nothing binds it to the caller. requireChannelAuthorIsMember (commandInvariants.ts:115-131) asks only 'is this authorRef SOME member', never 'is this authorRef the CALLER'. No caller identity reaches decideOrchestrationCommand at all - its inputs are {command, readModel}. Observed: a post supplying authorRef {memberKind human, memberId human-walt} was accepted and stamped authorHandle 'walt'. The contract comment at orchestration.ts:476 says 'Derived server-side, never supplied by an agent' and the decider comment calls itself 'the enforcement point every caller inherits'. Neither is true. A doc comment asserting an invariant that no code checks is the failure mode.

SEC-2 - MEMBERSHIP HAS NO AUTHZ AT ALL. channel.member.add checks only handle uniqueness; channel.member.remove checks only that the handle is present. Neither asks who is issuing. Observed: self-add by an unrelated caller -> Success; removing a rival member -> Success. Membership is the authz boundary for the entire comms layer (posting is gated on it, and the gateway gates reads on it), so an unguarded self-add is a self-service grant of post and read rights on any channel whose id you can name, and an unguarded remove silently evicts a peer from the wake set.

WHY IT IS NOT EXPLOITABLE TODAY, and why that is not comfort: channel.* commands were added to DispatchableClientOrchestrationCommand but NOT to ClientOrchestrationCommand, which is the schema rpc.ts:1161 actually decodes on the wire - verified. And the MCP gateway's createPost is still Effect.die(notWired). So the only thing standing between this and exploitation is a union that the integration task plausibly extends, plus an unimplemented method. The protection is ACCIDENTAL, not designed.

BLOCKS t3_bot-0uq (toolkit + live gateway registration) and t3_bot-75k (the post->turn reactor). Those are the two changes that open the surface. Do not land either until this is decided.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA - observable behaviour, not mechanism:
1. A caller supplying an authorRef that is not its own identity is REJECTED. Demonstrated by a test that constructs such a command and asserts failure - not by a comment saying it cannot happen.
2. channel.member.add and channel.member.remove issued by a caller with no standing in the target channel are REJECTED. Same demonstration standard.
3. Whatever mechanism is chosen, the wire exclusion stops being load-bearing by accident: either channel commands are deliberately absent from ClientOrchestrationCommand with a comment saying why and a test asserting they do not decode, or they are present and fully authorized.

DESIGN NOTE, because the obvious fix does not work: the decider cannot enforce this as currently shaped - it is pure and takes no caller identity, deliberately. Options are (a) strip authorRef from the command and have the engine stamp it from the dispatching credential before the decider runs, or (b) give the decider an explicit caller-identity parameter. (a) keeps the decider pure and is probably right; (b) is a signature change across every command. This is an architecture call, not a line edit - which is why it is a bead and not a fix inside yyd.
design: RULING (pm 22:20, criterion 3 amended 22:22 per boss1): Option A. The CommandEnvelope gains an engine-stamped issuer: MemberRef ({memberKind: human, memberId} for RPC clients; {memberKind: thread, memberId: threadId} for MCP-credentialed calls; system for seeds/reactors). Entry points stamp it; the wire schema (ClientOrchestrationCommand) does not carry it; the engine OVERWRITES any supplied value — never rejects, because a rejection reveals the field. channel.post.create carries NO authorRef — the decider reads command.issuer and stamps authorHandle from it. Membership changes (member.add/remove, meta.update, archive) are allowed only for issuer.memberKind in {human, system} for M1; a thread issuer is rejected with a typed error. Acceptance (executed probes): (1) an MCP-credentialed call posting with any spoofed author/issuer lands with authorHandle = the credential's thread, never the supplied value; (2) a thread issuer calling member.add on any channel is rejected; a human issuer succeeds; (3) a wire command carrying an issuer key decodes successfully and the stamped issuer is the credential's, not the supplied one; (4) tests fail if the engine stops overwriting issuer.

title: Router/decider agreement is unchecked for the 15 commands whose probe the decider refuses
description:
Found and EXECUTED by the test-coverage lane during the second /review-pr pass on PR #3 (t3_bot-eas), after that PR closed the router half of the same defect class.

THE ASYMMETRY. OrchestrationEngine.routing.test.ts's agreement test compares two independent command-to-aggregate mappings: commandToAggregateRef (the router) and the literals the decider stamps on the events it emits. A disagreement refuses a legitimate replay of a command that already succeeded, because the idempotency check compares the router's answer against a receipt written from the decider's.

PR #3 derives a hazard set - commands whose payload carries BOTH a projectId and a threadId - and requires every member to be compared, by name. That derivation is correct for ROUTER misplacement: a single-id command cannot be mis-routed, because the compiler keeps it out of a branch that reads an id it does not have. There are exactly 2 such commands (thread.create, thread.pull-request.sync) and both are now compared.

It is NOT correct for DECIDER flips, and the test catches those too. A decider literal is just a string; any command can carry the wrong one, single-id or not. So the hazard the derived set scopes is narrower than the hazard the test detects, and 15 of 39 commands are still uncompared against it.

EXECUTED by the lane: flipping the aggregate literal at decider.ts:675 (thread.snooze - single-id, uncompared) leaves the full orchestration suite GREEN at 41 files / 540 tests. Same class as the defect PR #3 just closed, still invisible for the uncompared set.

WHY IT IS LOWER SEVERITY THAN THE ONE IT RESEMBLES: a decider flip is a deliberate edit to a literal, not the plausible mis-paste of a `case` label between adjacent switch branches that motivated the router work. The router half is now covered for all 39.

WHAT WAS DONE IN PR #3: one sentence on dualIdCommandTypes() stating the derived set scopes the ROUTER hazard only, so the next reader does not mistake an empty uncovered-set for full coverage against decider flips. That is documentation of the gap, not closure of it. This bead is the closure.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the wrong fix fails):
1. Every declared command MUST be compared, or named as uncompared. Widening dualIdCommandTypes() to return all declared types is the right SHAPE, but it fails immediately: 15 commands are skipped because the decider refuses their bare probe and they emit no events. Those need real payloads, and for the ones behind a projection guard, a seeded read model - sequencing, not data. A fix that only widens the derived set and leaves the skips will fail its own assertion.
2. It MUST go RED under a decider flip on a SINGLE-ID command. Use decider.ts:675 (thread.snooze) - the exact mutation the lane executed and observed green. If it stays green, nothing was closed.
3. It MUST still go red under the two mutations PR #3 already catches (router flip and decider flip on thread.pull-request.sync). A rewrite that trades one class for the other is not progress.
4. State the compared count before and after. "All 39 compared" asserted without a number is the claim this whole line of work exists to distrust.

Related: t3_bot-d0y (conflict path never driven through production dispatch). Different defect - that one is about reaching the error at all, this one is about the mappings that decide it.

title: Onboarding: bootstrap dev env, run server+web, read docs/internals, report engine aggregates
close_reason: Both seniors reported: env green, engine aggregates mapped (boss1), MCP injection + live-turn path mapped (boss3)

title: No test reaches OrchestrationCommandIdConflictError through the production dispatch path
description:
Found by the test-coverage lane during /review-pr on PR #3 (t3_bot-eas), and left out of that PR deliberately: the gap predates it and the PR does not widen it.

commandToAggregateRef's output is compared against a stored command receipt's aggregate to decide whether a replayed commandId is a genuine retry or a collision, raising OrchestrationCommandIdConflictError (OrchestrationEngine.ts:219-231). That comparison is the ONE production behaviour the routing result gates.

EXECUTED by the lane: `rg -n "OrchestrationCommandIdConflictError" apps packages -g '*.ts'` returns 7 hits, all in Errors.ts and OrchestrationEngine.ts. Zero in any test file. Nothing exercises the conflict path.

Why it matters more than it looks: the ACCEPTED receipt is stamped from the decider's event (OrchestrationEngine.ts:366) while the conflict check compares the ROUTER's answer (:221). If those two mappings disagree, a legitimate replay of a command that already succeeded is refused. PR #3 now asserts the two mappings agree for every declared command, which closes the divergence at the unit level — but nothing drives the conflict path itself through the production dispatch entry point.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the wrong fix fails):
1. The test MUST dispatch through the real engine (createOrchestrationSystem in OrchestrationEngine.test.ts), not call commandToAggregateRef or the receipt repository directly. A unit test of the comparison does not verify the assembled path and does not close this.
2. It MUST assert the error carries BOTH aggregate scopes — the receipt's and the command's — not merely that an OrchestrationCommandIdConflictError was raised. Every conflict produces the same tag, so a tag-only assertion is non-discriminating (boss1 hit exactly this with five channel rejection tests that all passed against a synthesised requireChannel).
3. It MUST go RED when the routing switch is mutated so a command's aggregate disagrees with the decider's. If the test passes with that mutation applied, it is not testing the conflict this bead is about.
4. State whether a replay that SHOULD succeed (same commandId, same aggregate) still succeeds. A fix that makes every replay conflict would satisfy 1-3 and be worse than the gap.

Not M1-blocking. Nothing in the channel work depends on it.

title: Table-driven test: assert every command type routes to its expected aggregate
description:
Found by the QA lane during /review-pr on PR #2 (t3_bot-l8i), mutation E; verified at source by boss1.

commandToAggregateRef uses 'command satisfies never' in its default branch. That proves EXHAUSTIVENESS (every command has some branch). It proves NOTHING about CORRECTNESS (that each command sits in the RIGHT branch).

Demonstrated: moving case 'thread.pull-request.sync' from the thread branch into the project branch gives server typecheck exit 0 / zero errors, engine test 29/29 pass, ThreadPullRequestReactor 13/13 pass. Fully GREEN. Cause: ThreadPullRequestSyncCommand (packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:1454-1459) carries BOTH threadId AND projectId, so command.projectId resolves in the project branch and the command is silently stamped aggregateKind 'project'.

Contrast: mutation D moved 'thread.create' (no projectId) into the project branch - tests went RED but typecheck was STILL exit 0. So even where something catches it, it is the suite, not the compiler.

Blast radius if it happens: a thread's events, command receipt, and hasEventAfter scope attach to a project aggregate. Same damage class as the original silent-misroute this PR set out to prevent.

Scope of the fix: a table-driven test over the OrchestrationCommand union asserting each command type maps to its expected aggregateKind/aggregateId. Needs commandToAggregateRef exported (currently module-local at apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationEngine.ts:73) or exercised through dispatch.

Deliberately NOT done in PR #2: it is new work, not a line-edit, and widening a 111-line PR to chase it is scope creep. The 39 hand-maintained case labels make this MORE valuable over time, not less - every added command is another chance to put a case in the wrong group.

title: Non-member and missing channel are indistinguishable only by convention, not by test
description:
Raised by boss1's 22:30 finding on the mention-error ordering leak (2b6d71ba0), checked against the comms toolkit, and it is the same family one step removed.

THE PROPERTY: a caller must not be able to tell "this channel does not exist" from "this channel exists and I am not in it". Both must produce the identical CommsChannelNotFoundError. Otherwise any agent holding a comms credential can enumerate private channel names by probing.

TODAY IT HOLDS STRUCTURALLY, which is stronger than boss1's case: membership is a PARAMETER of the lookup (channels.getChannelForMember(name, scope.threadId), handlers.ts:138), not a guard that runs after it, so a non-member gets Option.none and falls into the SAME single branch as a missing channel (handlers.ts:143-145). There is no ordering to swap. That is the design and it should be preserved deliberately rather than by accident.

THE GAP: handlers.test.ts:242 pins only the NON-MEMBER side. Its comment says "Same error a missing channel gives" and then hardcodes what it believes that error to be. Nothing drives a channel that simply does not exist and compares. So the divergence is reachable from the other direction: change the MISSING-channel branch - add a reason field, a distinct tag, a different channel value - and the non-member test stays green while the two errors become distinguishable. The security property is asserted in a comment and checked on one side.

This becomes live rather than theoretical when the gateway gains a typed "exists but not a member" result, which is a natural thing to want for auditing. At that point mapping it to its own tool error is the obvious change and nothing stops it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the wrong fix fails):
1. The test MUST drive BOTH cases through the real handler in one test and assert the two errors are equal to each other - not each equal to a hardcoded literal. Two tests that each pin their own expected shape do not pin the relationship; that is the current state and it is what lets the two drift apart.
2. The comparison MUST be over the whole error value, not a _tag match. Every distinguishable variant this is guarding against shares the tag; a toMatchObject with only _tag passes against the exact leak it is supposed to prevent.
3. It MUST go RED when the missing-channel branch is mutated to carry any distinguishing field. Apply that mutation and record the output in the PR.
4. State whether a member asking for a channel that DOES exist still gets it. A fix that collapses every lookup to not-found would satisfy 1-3 and break the toolkit.

Not M1-blocking. The property holds today; this pins it so it keeps holding.

title: Channel-watch triggering: wake channel members on any post (post-M1; needs damping beyond never-wake-author)
Post-triggered turn on a busy Claude thread emits no turn.started
description:
ClaudeAdapter.sendTurn (apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:4892) treats a sendTurn during a live non-synthetic turn as a steer: it reuses the existing turnId, emits no turn.started event, and offers the message onto the session promptQueue (line 5018). A channel post that wakes a mid-turn agent is folded into the in-flight turn and has no turn of its own. Codex differs: CodexSessionRuntime.ts:2343 gets a distinct queued turn id back from turn/start but keeps activeTurnId pinned to the running turn. Found during t3_bot-c6z recon (Boss3).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the WRONG fix fails):
1. DO NOT fix this by emitting a synthetic turn.started. Fabricating a turn boundary the provider never produced makes the turn record lie about what the provider did, and the projector settles turns from provider session status — a synthetic start would corrupt duration and settlement. Reject any change that adds one.
2. Per-post identity in the channel view MUST key on the post/mention id, never on turnId. A post steered into a live turn shares that turn's id with other posts by construction.
3. TEST: deliver a post to a thread with a live non-synthetic turn and assert the post remains individually identifiable afterwards. Asserting that a turnId exists is NOT sufficient — it passes with the defect present, because the steered post does have a turnId; it just is not its own.
4. State the Codex behaviour explicitly in whatever the UI consumes, so the two providers do not silently differ in what a 'turn' means to the channel view.

title: Unrouted command path writes no command receipt (and has no counter of its own)
description:
Found by blind verification's adversarial pass on PR #2 (t3_bot-l8i), items 4/5, then refined after a partial disagreement from the verifier that changes how this must be fixed.

WHAT IS TRUE, UNQUALIFIED - the idempotency half:
After PR #2, commandToAggregateRef returns null for an unrouted command and processEnvelope early-returns before Effect.exit, so NO status:rejected receipt is written (observed: receipt_for_unrouted -> Option None). Main DID write one: its catch-all routed the command to thread, the decider then rejected it with OrchestrationCommandInvariantError, and the engine's failure branch wrote the receipt. That receipt short-circuits a replay of the same commandId; without it the command re-processes on every retry. This is a real contract difference.

WHAT IS NOT TRUE, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG - the telemetry half:
Do NOT write this up as 'we lost observability on the unrouted path' and do NOT restore the counter the way main emitted it. Main had no unrouted path at all. What main metered was a successfully-routed THREAD command - aggregateKind 'thread' with an aggregateId of whatever thread the payload happened to name - which the decider then rejected. That is MISATTRIBUTED telemetry, not observability. An operator reading it sees an elevated thread-command failure rate pointing at a specific innocent thread; they never see 'a command was unroutable'.

So the branch lost WRONG data. For a counter anyone alerts on, wrong attribution is plausibly worse than absence: it inflates a real metric and sends the investigation at the wrong aggregate. The regression is in telemetry VOLUME, not telemetry QUALITY.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, written to stop this being closed the wrong way:
1. Restore the rejected-receipt write for the unrouted path, so replay short-circuits as it does for every other rejection.
2. If a counter is added, it must be a signal OF ITS OWN identifying an unrouted command. It must NOT reuse main's shape (aggregateKind 'thread' + a payload-derived aggregateId). A fix that reintroduces the misattribution is a regression dressed as a fix.
3. CLAUDE.md requires stated motivation for instrumenting a statically unreachable branch. The motivation: if a build-time escape ever makes it reachable, an operator has no signal at all.

PRIORITY CONTEXT - why this is a bead and not a blocker on #2:
On main that path is REACHABLE (a threadId-bearing channel command compiles straight into the catch-all and misroutes silently - the exact defect #2 closes). On this branch it cannot compile: TS1360 at OrchestrationEngine.ts and at decider.ts. The gap sits on a path strictly harder to reach than the one it replaced, and the dispatching caller still receives a typed failure, so it is not silent to the client.

SEQUENCE, for anyone reconstructing this later: main (silent misrouting, survivable) -> 75328cd0b (compile-time exhaustiveness, FATAL at runtime - killed the worker fiber) -> d46a978a8 (compile-time exhaustiveness, survivable). The fiber-kill was introduced and closed within this PR; it was never on main.

title: Channel aggregate kind: add 'channel' to OrchestrationAggregateKind, widen aggregateId, make commandToAggregateRef exhaustive (no default)
Agent-originated turn dropped when thread is compacting
description:
ProviderCommandReactor.ts:1521 queues thread.turn-start-requested events into turnsAfterCompaction while a thread compacts, and cancelTurnsAfterCompaction discards them on compaction failure with a human-facing 'Send this message again to continue.' message. A turn triggered by a channel post has no human to resend it, so the post is silently dropped. Found during t3_bot-c6z recon (Boss3).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the WRONG fix fails):
1. A post-triggered turn cancelled by compaction failure MUST become OBSERVABLE — re-enqueued, or the originating post marked failed somewhere its author and the channel view can see. 'It no longer reaches the human-facing message' is NOT sufficient; silence is the defect, not the wording.
2. The fix MUST NOT reuse the existing human-facing instruction for an agent-originated turn. Telling a reader who does not exist to retry is the same bug with better copy.
3. Any retry MUST be bounded and the bound MUST be stated. An unbounded re-enqueue turns a compaction failure into a wake loop, which is the failure mode t3_bot-64d exists to cap.
4. TEST: drive an actual compaction failure with a post-triggered turn queued behind it and assert the turn is re-enqueued OR surfaced as failed. A test that asserts only that cancelTurnsAfterCompaction was called is tautological — it passes with the defect fully present.
5. Distinguish agent-originated from human-originated turns at the point of cancellation, or state why one path serves both.
close_reason: Not a bug: cancelTurnsAfterCompaction appends an error activity keyed by requestId (tested). Requirement moved into 75k criteria.

title: pnpm-lock.yaml drifts deterministically on every pnpm run (alchemy@2.0.0-beta.76 peer hash in infra/relay); regenerate deliberately in its own change
Channel aggregate: channel/membership/post/mention in OrchestrationEngine
Pin node to ^24.13.1 or relax engines; engine-strict is off so mismatch is silent
CI: upstream workflows target blacksmith-* runners the fork lacks; every job queues forever. Port ci.yml Check/Test jobs to ubuntu-latest or disable
rigor toolkit: RIGOR_UI_RE 'tsx?' matches plain .ts so every TS PR fires the Design lane (skills_library, not this repo)
Channel decider+projector+persistence: channel.*/membership/post events, ProjectionChannels repo, migration 051, post bodies in projection table
design:
PROJECTION SHAPE, derived from the ChannelGateway seam boss3 landed (apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/comms/channelGateway.ts). Read the seam before changing any of this - it is the contract, not a suggestion.

Four operations the projection must answer cheaply:

1. getChannelForMember(name, threadId) -> Option<Channel>
   Needs a channel lookup BY NAME plus a membership test for a memberId. So: unique index on channel name, and an index on membership(memberId) - this is the one place memberId is the right key. Note the seam requires a non-member and a non-existent channel to be INDISTINGUISHABLE: an agent must not be able to probe for channels it is not in. Do not return a different error for the two cases.
   Channel carries its full members array, so this read joins membership.

2. getPost(channelId, postId) -> Option<ChannelPostRecord>
   Point lookup scoped BY CHANNEL. A post in another channel returns None, same as missing. Exists so reply can validate a parent without paging history - a lookback bounded by page size silently refuses replies to older posts.

3. readPosts({channelId, limit, cursor}) -> {posts, nextCursor}
   Oldest first, ASCENDING by sequence. Cursor is opaque and points AFTER the last post returned. nextCursor null when no newer posts exist. limit is a maximum, not an exact count (1..200, enforced at the tool schema; the gateway may assume the range).
   So posts need a monotonic per-channel ordering column the cursor encodes. Use the event sequence.

4. createPost(input) -> {postId, createdAt}
   Typed failures: ChannelStoreUnavailable | ChannelWriteConflict | ChannelMembershipRevoked | ChannelMentionUnresolvable.
   The DECIDER is the enforcement point for the last two (pm ruling 184735): reject a post from a non-member, and reject a post carrying a mention that does not resolve to a current member - rejected WHOLE, never silently dropping the mention, because a post that drops a mention wakes nobody while looking sent. The toolkit's pre-check is for the agent-readable error; the aggregate is the guarantee, since the check and the write are not atomic.

POST RECORD FIELDS (ChannelPostRecord): postId, authorHandle, body, mentions (handles), parentPostId, createdAt.
Note authorHANDLE, not authorRef, on the read side - the gateway never exposes memberId to the agent. The event payload carries authorRef AND authorHandle; the projection serves the handle.

BRANDING, flagged by boss3 in the seam header: ids are plain string there as a staged simplification. When the aggregate brands them, ChannelMemberHandle surfaces in handlers.ts (mention resolution) and tools.ts (what the agent sends/receives). The compiler finds every site, but the landing spans more than the aggregate - coordinate with boss3 rather than branding unilaterally.

ROUTING HAZARD, learned in l8i: no channel.* command payload may carry a top-level field named threadId. A thread member's memberId IS a ThreadId, but naming the field threadId routes the command to the THREAD aggregate silently (commandToAggregateRef reads command.threadId). The seam's ChannelMember comment says the same thing. Field is memberId, always.
notes:
POST-MERGE WORK I OWE, in order:

1. ROUTING TABLE ROWS (after PR #3 merges; pm ruling 220709 fixed the order as #3 then #4).
Add seven rows to EXPECTED_AGGREGATE in apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationEngine.routing.test.ts:
  channel.create / channel.meta.update / channel.archive / channel.unarchive /
  channel.member.add / channel.member.remove / channel.post.create  -> all "channel"

THREE CORRECTIONS FROM boss3 (222649 then 222913). The third supersedes my own first plan, which was wrong
in the same way as the thing it was meant to fix.

(a) ASSERT THE COMPARED SET BY NAME, NOT THE COUNT. My plan was "confirm the compared-count is seven". That
passes if SEVEN commands were compared - not if MY seven were. Identical today, since seven is all the
channel commands there are; it stops being identical the moment an eighth lands or one of mine drops out and
an unrelated thread command drops in. Assert by name so the failure says WHICH command went uncompared:
  const uncovered = expectedSet.filter((type) => !compared.includes(type));
  expect(uncovered).toEqual([]);

(b) THE DERIVED HAZARD SET WILL NOT COVER MY SEVEN, and that is correct. It selects commands carrying BOTH
projectId and threadId; mine carry channelId alone, so the compiler already keeps them out of the wrong
branch. I need my own explicit expected set. If I assume the derivation picks them up I get an
empty-uncovered green for free and it means nothing.

(c) PROBE_EXTRAS CANNOT SATISFY requireChannel, which is where my first note was wrong. PROBE_EXTRAS only
enriches the command PAYLOAD; requireChannel reads the PROJECTION. No payload field can satisfy it. The probe
must DISPATCH channel.create first and let the projector land the channel before the other six are driven,
and post.create additionally needs a member.add to land first for the author check. That is a SEQUENCING
change to the test, not a data change.
And do not leave the sequence implicit: if channel.create silently fails, the six that follow all get
skipped and the false green returns in a new costume. ASSERT the channel is in the read model before the loop.

Only channel.create passes on a bare probe. The other six all call requireChannel first.

2. t3_bot-a44 (P0, mine, immediately after #4 merges) - engine-stamped issuer, authorRef leaves the command.

WHY BOTH ROUTING TESTS STAY: boss3 is EXECUTED over a subset - reads aggregateKind off the events the decider
actually emitted, catching a literal that is right in source and wrong after computation. The bug-lane check
is STATIC over the whole surface - reads the literals, covering commands nothing can currently drive. Neither
subsumes the other.

title: Decide explicitly whether the projector keeps forward-compatibility for *-requested events
description:
REWRITTEN after the history lane on PR #4 (HIST-1) showed my original framing was wrong. Read this before acting; the original would have produced six meaningless cases and silently contradicted a standing test.

WHAT I ORIGINALLY FILED: 'the projector default silently drops unhandled events; make it exhaustive'. I filed that after channel events typechecked clean while being dropped, and I assumed the catch-all was an oversight.

WHY THAT WAS WRONG: the default is DELIBERATE and pinned by name. History: introduced by 483a1ae371 (Julius Marminge, 2026-02-21) when the file was reducer.ts; 25d20ab792 (2026-02-24) added projector.test.ts:302, a test called 'keeps projector forward-compatible for unhandled event types' which drives thread.turn-start-requested through projectEvent and asserts the model is unchanged. That test has stood ~7 months.

WHAT ACTUALLY FALLS THROUGH TODAY: exactly six event types, and they form one coherent category - every *-requested event: thread.turn-start-requested, thread.turn-interrupt-requested, thread.approval-response-requested, thread.user-input-response-requested, thread.checkpoint-revert-requested, thread.session-stop-requested. They are reactor triggers with no read-model effect (thread.turn-start-requested is consumed by CheckpointReactor) and have NEVER been cased in projector.ts or its reducer.ts ancestor.

So making projectEvent exhaustive would force six 'case ...: return nextBase' entries whose only content is the fall-through the default already expresses, AND would contradict the intent that test pins by name.

THE REAL QUESTION, which is a decision and not a defect: is forward-compatibility for unhandled event types still wanted? The catch-all's cost is that a NEW event type is silently ignored, which is how the channel events nearly shipped unprojected. Its benefit is that reactor-trigger events need no projector ceremony.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Read projector.test.ts:302 and decide explicitly: retained or revoked.
2. If REVOKED: the exhaustive switch and the deletion/rewrite of that test land in the SAME change. Leaving the test while adding six no-op cases makes it assert nothing.
3. If RETAINED: no code change. Record the decision where the next person meets it - a comment at the default branch naming the *-requested category and why it is ignored - so the next new event type does not get dropped by a reader who thinks the default is an oversight, as I did.

PR #4 needs no change either way. Its seven explicit channel cases are additive, and the inline comment explaining why channel.post-created is cased rather than defaulted is the right treatment.

title: Channel events are a replay one-way door: old binaries fail bootstrap on aggregateKind=channel
description:
Found by the Contracts lane during /review-pr on PR #2 (t3_bot-l8i). RESOLVED as a decision by boss1 before starting yyd. Read the CORRECTION below before acting - my original framing offered a fix that does not work.

THE FAILURE, unchanged and real:
A pre-channel binary's OrchestrationAggregateKind is Schema.Literals(['project','thread']) and REJECTS aggregateKind 'channel'. OrchestrationEventStore.readFromSequence decodes rows via Effect.forEach(rows, decodeEvent) - fail-fast, no per-row tolerance, and it does NOT use the repo's own ForwardCompatibleArray (baseSchemas.ts:85). ProjectionPipeline.bootstrapProjector replays from sequence 0 at startup. So ONE undecodable row fails the whole environment bootstrap, not just one read. Same shape as the attachment replay limit documented in docs/internals/providers.md.

CORRECTION - option (a) in my original description was a CATEGORY ERROR. Do not implement it.
I originally offered 'advertise a channels capability on the environment descriptor and negotiate it the way pull-request linking does'. That does NOT fix this. Verified: capabilities are hardcoded in the server's own descriptor (apps/server/src/environment/ServerEnvironment.ts:215-240, e.g. threadPullRequests: true) and are sent to CLIENTS over RPC to tell them what this server supports. Nothing in the replay path consults them. A server advertising channels:false still has to decode whatever is already in its own SQLite at boot, and still dies on the row. The capability pattern solves CLIENT-vs-SERVER skew; this is an OLD-BINARY-READS-NEW-ROWS problem on a different axis entirely. Implementing the flag would look like a fix, pass review, and leave the failure exactly where it was.

THE REAL OPTIONS ARE ONLY TWO:
(1) Make the event-store decode tolerant - skip or quarantine rows whose type/kind this binary does not know, so an unknown aggregate degrades instead of bricking boot. This is the durable fix and it is where ForwardCompatibleArray would belong. It is also a change to the replay path shared by every aggregate, so it is NOT M1 work.
(2) Accept it as a one-way door and write it down.

DECISION FOR M1: option (2). Channel events are a one-way door. Once an environment has written one, it cannot be downgraded to a pre-channel binary without failing to start.
Rationale: M1 runs one binary on one machine (Walt's), so realised downgrade risk is near zero, and AGENTS.md says design for current requirements only. Option (1) is real machinery on a path shared by every aggregate, and buying it now to protect a scenario M1 does not have is exactly the 'introduce machinery because it looks architecturally impressive' that AGENTS.md warns against.
CONDITION THAT REOPENS THIS: the moment channels ship anywhere with independently-upgrading environments - upstream, a relay/tunnel host, or a desktop build users can roll back - option (2) stops being acceptable and option (1) becomes required. That is a real one-way door and it should be a conscious crossing, not a discovery.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- docs/internals states channel events are a one-way door with no supported downgrade, and says why the capability descriptor does not address it (so the category error is not re-derived).
- Do NOT add a 'channels' capability flag believing it solves replay.
- yyd may proceed on this decision.
